t: LeetCode 1435 — Create a Session Bar Chart
o: We must bucket each session's `duration` (in seconds) into four fixed bins based on minutes: [0-5), [5-10), [10-15), and '15 or more', then report each bin label with its session count — including bins with zero sessions. In Example 1, durations 30s, 199s, 299s fall under 5 minutes (3 sessions), 580s falls in [5-10> (1 session), nothing lands in [10-15>, and 1000s is 15 or more. The key subtlety is that every bin must appear exactly once even when its count is 0, so we cannot simply GROUP BY the computed bin over the Sessions table alone — we need all four bins to exist independently of the data.
k: Convert seconds to minutes by integer division: duration / 60 gives the minute value used for bucketing.
A plain GROUP BY on the bucket expression drops empty bins; cross joining (or UNION-ing) the four fixed bins guarantees they all appear.
CASE WHEN or arithmetic like LEAST(FLOOR(duration/60),15)/5 can map any duration to one of four buckets.

a.n: Approach 1: CASE WHEN with UNION of fixed bins
a.i: Compute each session's bin label with a CASE expression, aggregate counts per label, then LEFT JOIN (or UNION-combine) against a hardcoded list of the four bins so zero-count bins still show up. This is the most readable and directly mirrors the problem statement.
s: Define the four bin labels as a derived table Bins.
For each session, compute its label via CASE on duration/60 (<5, <10, <15, else).
Group sessions by label and count them into a derived table Counts.
LEFT JOIN Bins with Counts and use IFNULL(count, 0) so missing bins report 0.

c.python:
-- Database problem: submit this MySQL query.
SELECT b.bin,
       IFNULL(c.total, 0) AS total
FROM (
    SELECT '[0-5>' AS bin
    UNION ALL SELECT '[5-10>'
    UNION ALL SELECT '[10-15>'
    UNION ALL SELECT '15 or more'
) b
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT CASE
               WHEN duration / 60 < 5 THEN '[0-5>'
               WHEN duration / 60 < 10 THEN '[5-10>'
               WHEN duration / 60 < 15 THEN '[10-15>'
               ELSE '15 or more'
           END AS bin,
           COUNT(*) AS total
    FROM Sessions
    GROUP BY 1
) c ON b.bin = c.bin;

a.n: Approach 2: Arithmetic bucketing with SUM aggregation
a.i: Instead of grouping by a string label, compute a bucket index from minutes via LEAST(FLOOR(duration/60), 15) DIV 5, giving indices 0..3. Cross join Sessions with the fixed bins and conditionally sum matches — no join keys on strings needed and no risk of dropped groups.
s: Cross join the 4-row Bins table with Sessions.
Map each session to index FLOOR(duration/60) capped at 15, divided by 5.
For each bin row, SUM whether the session's index equals the bin's index.
Select bin label and that conditional sum as total.

c.python:
-- Database problem: submit this MySQL query.
SELECT b.bin,
       SUM(FLOOR(s.duration / 300) = b.idx) AS total
FROM (
    SELECT 0 AS idx, '[0-5>' AS bin
    UNION ALL SELECT 1, '[5-10>'
    UNION ALL SELECT 2, '[10-15>'
    UNION ALL SELECT 3, '15 or more'
) b
CROSS JOIN Sessions s
GROUP BY b.idx, b.bin
ORDER BY b.idx;

w: In an interview, lead with Approach 1 since it reads naturally, then mention Approach 2 as a slicker arithmetic variant. The classic pitfall is writing a simple GROUP BY on the CASE label and losing bins with zero sessions — always anchor your answer to an explicit list of all four bins. Watch boundary conditions: 300 seconds belongs to [5-10>, not [0-5>, because bins are half-open; integer division duration/60 handles this correctly. Likely follow-ups: generalize to k variable-width bins stored in a ranges table (join on duration >= start AND duration < end), or produce the chart ordered by bin.
